$comment: P63 [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNMENT-CEILING-REFUSES-WHAT-TWO-REFERENCES-RUN]], the NEGATIVE half: a statically allocated object over-aligned beyond what the OUTPUT FORMAT can place it at is refused BY NAME, never placed misaligned. MEASURED 2026-09-07 with the requestable ceiling raised and this gate ABSENT: the very same program built rc 0 on pe64 and the FIRST over-aligned static failed its own `% 8192` check at run time (exit 50) -- a clean build with a misplaced object, the silent miscompile this gate exists to prevent. A single over-aligned object at the head of a section can be right BY LUCK, which is why the program carries two of them behind odd-sized fillers. $$ THE UNION SAYS THE CEILING IS REAL AND WHERE: mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 refuses a PE static above 8192 ("alignment of 'g' is greater than maximum object file alignment 8192") and MSVC 19.51 refuses `__declspec(align(16384))` with `error C2345` -- both probed SEPARATELY, both landing on PE's own encoding limit. $$ THE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE IT A STATEMENT ABOUT STORAGE RATHER THAN ABOUT ALIGNMENT: the SAME mingw compiler at the SAME value BUILDS AND RUNS the request on a TYPE and on an AUTOMATIC object (MEASURED, exit 42 for both at 16384 and 65536). So this ceiling belongs to the format writer and must never move into the semantic ladder, where it would refuse `aligned(65536)` types every reference runs. $ THE BOUND IS THE FORMAT DOCUMENT'S OWN DECLARED `optionalHeader.sectionAlignment` (4096), read at emit time -- raising the document raises the ceiling with no code change. $ PE ONLY, and that is measured rather than conservative: on `elf64-x86_64-linux-exec` the identical program places all four objects correctly at 8192, 16384 and 65536 (run under WSL, exit 42), so an ELF gate would refuse what DSS demonstrably gets right. `positioned: false` because a link-tier diagnostic carries no source span.
